dedupe_keys.name: onthemap for emergency management population and workforce in live hazard areas

description: OnTheMap for Emergency Management is a free web application of the U.S. Census Bureau's Center for Economic Studies that overlays current hazard event areas on Census population and workforce statistics, so users can see who lives and works inside an event footprint. Event layers are loaded automatically for tropical storms (current wind radii, cumulative wind swath and forecast cone), wildfire perimeters, likely and observed floods, winter weather (forecast snowfall and freezing rain) and federal emergency or disaster declaration areas. For an event area or user-selected areas, it reports 2020-2024 ACS characteristics, 2020 census counts and 2023 LODES workforce statistics for workers living and employed in the area, including where those workers commute to and from; tabulations carry derived estimates and margins of error. Coverage: the United States; ACS and LODES inputs were updated on March 4, 2026. Access: browser application with export and share functions; the Emergency Management Hub on census.gov gathers it with the Census Business Builder quick lookup, Community Resilience Estimates and other tools; free, public domain statistics. Caveats: event geometries come from outside agencies and change during an event; some cells are suppressed for confidentiality; it is not open-source and has no documented bulk API. Simulation uses: rapid exposure estimates of residents and workers inside storm, flood and wildfire footprints for emergency response planning, and scenario inputs for evacuation and business interruption models. Related records: LODES and OnTheMap, Community Resilience Estimates, My Community Explorer and the FEMA National Risk Index.
